events.title: Gore carries Maine
events.text: Maine voted Democratic for president by five points, as it has in every election since 1992.

events.title: Collins's second term
events.text: Susan Collins, first elected in 1996, won a second term in the U.S. Senate.

events.title: Jackson elected
events.text: Troy Jackson, a logger from Allagash, won a Maine House seat as an independent; he became a Democrat in 2004.

events.title: Collins's third term
events.text: Collins was re-elected while Barack Obama carried Maine by seventeen points.

events.title: Jackson in the Senate
events.text: Jackson moved to the Maine Senate, where he served until 2014 and again from 2016 to 2024.

events.title: LePage elected
events.text: Republican Paul LePage won the governorship with 37.6 percent in a three-way race.

events.title: King to the Senate
events.text: Former governor Angus King, an independent, was elected to the U.S. Senate; he caucuses with the Democrats.

events.title: Bucksport mill closes
events.text: The Verso paper mill in Bucksport closed after 84 years, with 570 jobs lost.

events.title: Collins's fourth term
events.text: Collins was re-elected for a fourth term.

events.title: Ranked choice approved
events.text: Maine voters approved ranked-choice voting in a referendum, with about 52 percent.

events.title: A split electoral vote
events.text: Hillary Clinton carried Maine, but Donald Trump carried the 2nd District and its electoral vote.

events.title: Madison mill stops
events.text: The Madison paper mill stopped production, the state's fifth major mill closure in three years.

events.title: First ranked count
events.text: Jared Golden trailed in the first round in the 2nd District but won the final round, 50.6 to 49.4 percent.

events.title: Kavanaugh vote
events.text: Collins voted to confirm Brett Kavanaugh to the Supreme Court, after a Senate speech explaining her vote.

events.title: Senate President
events.text: Jackson became President of the Maine Senate, serving until December 2024.

events.title: Collins re-elected
events.text: Collins won a fifth term with 51.0 percent to Sara Gideon's 42.4: a first-round majority, so no ranked count.

events.title: Ticket splitting
events.text: On the same ballot, Joe Biden carried Maine by 9.1 points; Maine was the only state to split its president and Senate results.

events.title: A vote to convict
events.text: Collins voted to convict Donald Trump at his second impeachment trial.

events.title: Jay mill closes
events.text: Production ended at the Androscoggin Mill in Jay, three years after an explosion destroyed its digester.

events.title: Golden's narrow win
events.text: Golden held the 2nd District after a ranked count and a recount, 50.35 to 49.65 percent.

events.title: Harris carries Maine
events.text: Kamala Harris won Maine by 6.9 points; Trump carried the 2nd District by about nine.

events.title: Votes against nominees
events.text: Collins voted against Pete Hegseth for Defense Secretary and Kash Patel for FBI Director.

events.title: Medicaid vote
events.text: Collins voted against the final passage of President Trump's tax-and-spending law, citing its Medicaid cuts.

events.title: Jackson runs for governor
events.text: Jackson launched a campaign for governor at the Portsmouth Naval Shipyard in Kittery.

events.title: Platner launches
events.text: Graham Platner, an oyster farmer and veteran from Sullivan, entered the Democratic Senate primary.

events.title: Portland rally
events.text: About 6,500 people joined Platner and Senator Bernie Sanders at a Labor Day rally in Portland.

events.title: Mills enters
events.text: Governor Janet Mills joined the Democratic Senate primary.

events.title: Old posts surface
events.text: CNN and other outlets reported Platner's deleted Reddit posts; he apologised in a video the next day.

events.title: Tattoo covered
events.text: Platner had a tattoo resembling a Nazi symbol covered, saying he had not known what it resembled.

events.title: Collins runs again
events.text: Collins announced her campaign for a sixth term.

events.title: Mills withdraws
events.text: Mills suspended her campaign, citing a lack of money; her name stayed on the ballot.

events.title: Ten thousand votes
events.text: Collins cast her ten-thousandth consecutive roll-call vote; she has not missed one since 1997.

events.title: Platner wins primary
events.text: Platner won the Democratic primary with about 72 percent of the vote.

events.title: Jackson third
events.text: In the ranked count for the Democratic governor nomination, Jackson was eliminated in the third round.

events.title: Allegation published
events.text: Politico published a former partner's allegation that Platner sexually assaulted her in 2021; he denied it.

events.title: Party leaders react
events.text: Senate Democratic leaders, the Maine Democratic Party and Senator Sanders called on Platner to step aside.

events.title: Platner withdraws
events.text: Platner suspended his campaign on 8 July and formally withdrew on 10 July.

events.title: Jackson nominated
events.text: At a convention in Bangor, Democratic delegates chose Jackson, 566 votes to 5.

events.title: Six write-ins
events.text: Six write-in candidates declared, so the Senate race will go to a ranked count if no one wins a majority.

events.title: Four debates
events.text: Collins and Jackson debated on 6 October in Portland, on 8 October in Westbrook, and on 13 and 15 October in Bangor.

events.title: Election Day
events.text: On 3 November Maine chooses between Collins and Jackson.

eras: Ranked choice and a divided state
chartNote: Each state is coloured by the margin of the most recent presidential popular vote (Democratic minus Republican share of all votes, from certified results). It is a simplification: Maine elects its senator in its own race, and many Mainers split their tickets (in 2020 Joe Biden carried Maine by 9.1 points while Susan Collins won by 8.6), and Maine's 2nd District has voted Republican for president since 2016 even as the state voted Democratic. So the presidential colour is a backdrop, not a forecast. Shares are of land area, not of people or votes. Boundaries are today's states (Natural Earth); the map is framed on Maine, so outer states are cut at the edge.
